title: VLANs and network segmentation
goal_html: Students design a VLAN segmentation scheme for a small office network, assign hosts to VLANs, and argue which traffic flows should be permitted or blocked. Ties to LO 3.3.A (explain how VLANs segment a network to reduce risk).
reference_html:
Printed host inventory (if no laptop)

Host Role
WS-01, WS-02 Employee workstations
PRT-01 Department printer
SRV-01 File server
SRV-02 HR payroll database
CAM-01 IP security camera
GUEST-01 Visitor laptop
MGMT-01 Network switch management interface
steps_html:
1. Each pair draws four VLAN boxes on paper (Management, Employee, Server, Guest/IoT) and assigns each host in the inventory to one VLAN. They must be ready to justify each placement.
  2. The pair writes three traffic flow statements (e.g., "WS-01 sends a file request to SRV-01") and decides: Allow or Block? They circle their answer and write one sentence of justification.
  3. Pairs open the simulation, enter their VLAN assignments, and run the test flows to see whether the sim agrees. For any disagreement, they revise their reasoning.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "network designer" (defends the VLAN placement), the other is the "red team analyst" (argues which flows an attacker would try first if they compromised GUEST-01). After step 3, swap roles and repeat with MGMT-01 as the hypothetical target.
exit_html: Each student submits: their finalized VLAN map (4 VLANs, all 7 hosts assigned) plus one sentence explaining why SRV-02 (payroll) should never be reachable from the Guest VLAN even if a firewall rule was accidentally left open.
